sentences.text: The Assistant Commissioner of Police, Jayanagar Sub- Division, Bangalore, has submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 and 2 for the offences punishable U/s.498A and 304B r/w Sec.34 of IPC and Sec.3 and 4 of DP Act in Crime No.128/2016 of J PNagar P.S., Bangalore 2.

The factual matrix of the case is that:
The marriage between the sister of informant by name Smt. Umadevi and accused No.1 was solemnized on 1.6.2012 at Sri Adiparashkathi Kalyana Mantapa,
Shakthinagar, Malur Town, Kolar District, as per the rites and customs prevails in their community.
At the time of marriage on demand the accused persons received gold articles as dowry from her parents.

After the marriage the the sister of informant started residing along with accused persons at House bearing No.37/2, I Floor, 12th Cross, Puttenahalli Grama, JP Nagar VII Phase, within the limits of JP Nagar P.S.,
Bangalore.

The accused No.1 and 2 subjected the sister of informant to physical and mental cruelty, and got pledged the gold articles given at the SC No.74/2017 time of marriage by demanding additional dowry in terms of Rs.1,00,000/- from her parents home.
The deceased-Smt. Umadevi has brought the same to the notice of CW.1 and CW.2, but they use to console her.

After lapse of one year deceased-Smt. Umadevi gave birth to a female child, and after the naming ceremony of the child, the parents of complainant have sent back the deceased-Smt. Umadevi and child to the house of accused No.1.

At that time the accused started to harass the deceased-Smt. Umadevi by demanding for additional dowry, by assalting ousted her from the matrimonial house, by feeling hurt, deceased-Smt. Umadevi returned to her parents house, and during the panchayath the accused persons have demanded additional dowry of Rs.1,00,000/-, and after advising the accused persons the parents of complainant have sent back the deceased-Umadevi to the house of accused.
Thereafter the accused No.1 and 2 continued to harass the deceased physically and mentally by demanding additional dowry.
Due to unbearable torture of accused persons both physically and mentally the deceased-Smt. Umadevi committed suicide on 12.03.2016 at her matrimonial home.

Accordingly, the case was registered against the accused persons for subjecting the deceased for mental and physical cruelty and abetting the deceased to commit suicide in demand of additional dowry within seven years from the date of marriage.

sentences.text: Prosecution failed to establish that the death of deceased-Smt. Umadevi is due to dowry harassment.
Supreme (Guj) 343 (Indrasing M Rao Vs., State) Hon'ble Gujarat High Court held that The meaning of cruelty is given vide explanation to Sec..498A.
It means willful conduct of such nature, as is likely propel, or goad or compel the women to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb of health.

If the women is subjected to harassment with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand, for property or valuable security or coercing and her relative owing to failure on her or her relatives part to meet such demand, the same would also amount to cruelty.
The expression cruelty means and implies harsh and harmful conduct of certain intensity and persistence.

It, therefore covers the acts causing both physical and mental agony and torture, or tyranny and harm as well as unending accusations and recrimination reflecting bitterness putting the victim thereof to intense miseries and owes strong stirring up her feeling that life is now not worth living and she should die, being the only option left.
The provision of Sec.498A therefore envisages intention to drag or force the women to commit suicide by unabetted, persistent and grave cruelty.

The meaning of word harass which can be found from the dictionary is to subject some one to unbearable, continuous or repeated or persistent unprovoked vexatious attacks, questions, demands or SC No.74/2017 persecutions or brutality, or tyranny or harm or pain or afflictions, or other unpleasantness, or grave annoyances or troubles.
In short what can be said is that Sec.498A will not come in to play in every case of harassment and/ or cruelty.
Reasonable nexus between cruelty and suicide must be established.

It should therefore be shown that the incessant harassment or cruelty was with a view to force the wife to end her life or fulfill illegal demands of her husband or in laws, and was not matrimonial cruelty namely usual wear and tear of matrimonial life.
It should be hardly stated that the prosecution has to establish the charge beyond reasonable doubt.

No doubt arithmetical accuracy is not expected from the prosecution, but it has to adduce such evidence which would be credible leaving no room to any reasonable doubt"and pointing to the guilt of the accused".
In the case on hand the brother and parents of the deceased examined on behalf of the prosecution deposed that there was no matrimonial dispute between the deceased and accused.
There is no evidence on record to establish that the accused persons received dowry from the parents of the deceased .

sentences.text: If Sec.304B of IPC r/w Sec.113B of Evidence Act

, a comprehensive picture emerges that if a married women dies in an unnatural circumstances at her matrimonial home within seven years from her marriage and there are allegations of cruelty or harassment upon such married women for or in connection with demand of dowry by the husband or relatives of the husband, the case would squarely come under dowry death and there shall be presumption against the husband and the relatives.

In order to hold an accused guilt of an offence U/s.304B of IPC it has to be shown that apart from the fact that the women died on account burn or bodily injury, otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, it has also to be shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband,
or in connection with any demand for dowry.

Only then would such death be called dowry death and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused death of women concerned as held in 2010 AIR SCW 3673(Durgaprasad and another Vs., State of AP).

entities.text: 2010 AIR SCW 3673(Durgaprasad and another Vs., State of AP)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in 2020(5) KCCR 905 (Mahalingappla Vs., State of Karnataka) held that death of victim within seven years from the date of marriage alone can not be ground to convict the accused.

Physical and mental harassment meted out by the deceased resulted in her suicide and receiving of dowry at SC No.74/2017 the time of marriage, demand for additional dowry after marriage has not been established by the prosecution with available evidence on record.
The prosecution has failed to establish the charge leveled against the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, I answer points No.1 to 4 in the Negative.
20. Point No.5:

In view of answer of court on points No.1 to 4, this court pass the following:-
ORDER Acting U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 and 2 are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.498A and 304B r/w Sec.34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3 and 4 of DP Act.
The bail and surety bonds of accused No.1 and 2 stand canceled.
MO1 being worthless shall be destroyed after appeal period is over.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Supreme (Guj) 343 (Indrasing M Rao Vs., State) Hon'ble Gujarat High Court held that The meaning of cruelty is given vide explanation to Sec..498A.
The expression cruelty means and implies harsh and harmful conduct of certain intensity and persistence.
It, therefore covers the acts causing both physical and mental agony and torture, or tyranny and harm as well as unending accusations and recrimination reflecting bitterness putting the victim thereof to intense miseries and owes strong stirring up her feeling that life is now not worth living and she should die, being the only option left.
The provision of Sec.498A therefore envisages intention to drag or force the women to commit suicide by unabetted, persistent and grave cruelty.
There is no evidence on record to establish that the accused persons received dowry from the parents of the deceased .
19.The basic ingredients to attract the provisions of Sec.304B are (i) the death of the women should be caused by burns or fatal injury or otherwise than under normal circumstances;
(ii) Such death should have occurred within seven years of her marriage SC No.74/2017 (iii) she must have been subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband;
(iv)such cruelty and harassment should be for in connection with demand for dowry.

7
If Sec.304B of IPC r/w Sec.113B of Evidence Act
, a comprehensive picture emerges that if a married women dies in an unnatural circumstances at her matrimonial home within seven years from her marriage and there are allegations of cruelty or harassment upon such married women for or in connection with demand of dowry by the husband or relatives of the husband, the case would squarely come under dowry death and there shall be presumption against the husband and the relatives.
In order to hold an accused guilt of an offence U/s.304B of IPC it has to be shown that apart from the fact that the women died on account burn or bodily injury, otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, it has also to be shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband,
or in connection with any demand for dowry.
Only then would such death be called dowry death and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused death of women concerned as held in 2010 AIR SCW 3673(Durgaprasad and another Vs., State of AP).
Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in 2020(5) KCCR 905 (Mahalingappla Vs., State of Karnataka) held that death of victim within seven years from the date of marriage alone can not be ground to convict the accused.
Physical and mental harassment meted out by the deceased resulted in her suicide and receiving of dowry at SC No.74/2017 the time of marriage, demand for additional dowry after marriage has not been established by the prosecution with available evidence on record.
The prosecution has failed to establish the charge leveled against the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
